The models

One recipe, two encoder sizes. Both keep the acoustic half of Whisper, drop the autoregressive decoder, and add pre-LN transformer blocks and a linear CTC head over one shared Italian and English vocabulary.

What both share

  • The same job: Italian speech with English terms inside it; lowercase, unpunctuated text.
  • Encoder-only CTC on a Whisper encoder, extra pre-LN blocks and a linear head over a 1,024-piece Italian and English BPE.
  • Silero VAD, beam 12, top-k 10, LM weight 0.55 and token bonus 2.7.
  • Record then transcribe, on CPU and in a browser tab; at most 30 seconds per pass.
  • Apache-2.0. Initial encoders from openai/whisper-tiny and openai/whisper-base (MIT).

Moth 0.8.1 Italian speech, English terms, one small package

Moth is a CTC speech-to-text model for the way Italians actually talk: Italian sentences with English words and phrases inside them. It is built on a Whisper-tiny encoder, ships as a 19.7 MB package, and transcribes in the browser through ONNX Runtime Web.

The package contains the whole model runtime: an 11.9 MB int8 ONNX graph, a 5.4 MB trigram language model, a 2.3 MB Silero VAD, the vocabulary and the mel filterbank. No PyTorch, no Python, no server. The browser path is ONNX Runtime Web over WASM, and the audio never leaves the tab.

It is record-then-transcribe, not streaming. It writes lowercase text without punctuation and spells numbers out. Pure English is not the use case; the model is for Italian speech with English terms embedded in it.

MOTH-50 0.9.8-e023-r1 The 50 MB Moth, with the same job

MOTH-50 is the second Moth: a 49.2 MB code-switching speech-to-text model built on a Whisper-base encoder, with six extra transformer blocks and a linear CTC head. It runs on CPU and in a browser tab, and the audio never leaves the machine.

Released on 2026-11-26 as 0.9.8-e023-r1, it keeps the same job and the same deployment contract as 0.8.1 — Italian speech with English terms inside, record then transcribe, on a CPU and in a browser tab — with a 50 MB ceiling instead of the 20 MB that shaped the first model.

The extra room buys a Whisper-base encoder with six additional transformer blocks and a linear CTC head: 39,259,649 acoustic parameters in a 40.0 MB int8 graph, 49,204,097 bytes for the whole package. It keeps the 1,024-piece Italian and English BPE, the Silero VAD and the same frozen decoder settings. The 0.9.8 release is a NOTICE-only repackaging of 0.9.7: graph, LM, VAD, vocabulary and mel filters are the same bytes.

On the repeated T-600 read it is 12.30 WER / 78.14 ETA, against 13.70 / 76.13 for Moth 0.8.1 with the same E-034c LM. The evidence is still scripted read speech from known voices; the model card records the full boundary.

The benchmarks

Same decoder settings and the published int8 packages. Lower WER is better; ETA is the share of annotated English-origin words reproduced exactly.

Read the split, not just the total

  • T-600 is a declared repeated read: 600 clips from three known voices, not a fresh holdout.
  • FLEURS and CS-FLEURS were read once, report-only, and never used to select anything.
  • CS-FLEURS is CC-BY-NC and test-only; its 176 utterances come from one speaker.
  • 0.8.1 was not evaluated on S1-dev or CS-FLEURS: those rows are marked not published and are MOTH-50 only.

Where each fails

The limits are the same shape at both sizes; the larger model narrows them, but it does not remove them.

Moth 0.8.1

  • Pure English is weak: 49.81 WER on FLEURS-EN. This is a code-switching model, not a bilingual one.
  • No punctuation, no casing, no formatting. Numbers are spelled out in Italian.
  • Speaker coverage is three people. S3 has no training audio and shares a recording setup with S1.
  • One training seed for the released model. The intervals are utterance-level bootstrap; training variance was not measured.
  • Music can produce words. The VAD stops silence and steady noise, not music.

MOTH-50

  • Pure English is still a check, not a use case: 28.1955 WER on FLEURS-EN.
  • CS-FLEURS-READ is one speaker and one read: 34.8085 WER, CC-BY-NC and test-only.
  • Scripted read speech, not spontaneous conversation. Not validated on far-field, strong accents, children or unseen dialects.
  • S1, S2 and S3 are known voices. S3 never trained, but the model was evaluated on it repeatedly.
  • No punctuation, no casing, no user glossary; at most 30 seconds per pass.

How they work

No neural decoder, no language token, no generation loop. The encoder sees the audio, the CTC head emits one distribution per frame, and the decoder turns that into words.

Listen at 50 frames a second.

Both models use Whisper's front-end: 80-bin log-mel at 16 kHz, a 25 ms window and a 10 ms hop. Two convolutions take the sequence to 50 frames per second.

Encode, then score every frame.

0.8.1 shares four pretrained Whisper-tiny blocks and two extra transformer blocks at width 384. MOTH-50 shares six Whisper-base blocks and six extra blocks at width 512. Both project each frame to 1,025 CTC tokens: blank plus a 1,024-piece Italian and English BPE.

Search the words, not the text.

Prefix beam search with beam 12, top-k 10, a trigram LM at weight 0.55 and a per-token bonus of 2.7. The bonus is not optional: without it the beam under-emits and deletes words.

Moth 0.8.1 path; MOTH-50 uses the same recipe with a larger encoder. Full model card

What comes back

Both packages use the same seven-file contract. The runtime verifies every sha256 and the declared budget before loading; the input is mono 16 kHz PCM in [-1, 1] and the output is lowercase, unpunctuated text.

The 0.8.1 paper

The 0.8.1 paper is a preprint in the moth-stt repository. It reports the 41-experiment development record behind the first release, including the interventions that were rejected, and it measures the costs a single headline number hides.

What the paper adds

  • INT8 costs 0.16 pp WER on the 3,939-clip dev set, against the same checkpoint in fp32.
  • The browser path costs 0.72 pp on T-600: WER / ETA 24.80 / 54.36 in Chromium against 24.08 / 55.23 in Python.
  • The three voices span 5.34 pp WER and 12.02 pp ETA.
  • Four seeds of a rejected recipe span 0.46 pp — the scale at which small acoustic differences should be read as noise.

Moth: A 19.7 MB Italian–English Code-Switching Speech Recognizer Built on a Pretrained Whisper-Tiny Encoder

Tancredi Bosi, Semantique · November 2026 · preprint

Moth initializes a Whisper-tiny encoder, adds two transformer blocks and a linear CTC head over one shared 1,024-piece Italian and English vocabulary, and drops the autoregressive decoder and the language token. The paper reports the 41 experiments behind that design, the 12 rejected interventions and the deployment costs: INT8, the browser path, speaker spread and seed variance.

The boundary is explicit: all code-switching quality evidence is scripted read speech from three known voices, and the paper makes no claim of spontaneous code-switching or unseen-speaker generalization.
